answer: Quadratic influence weighting makes splitting one track record into many identities a losing trade. A seat's jury vote counts as R squared, where R is the number of answers it passed on its own key in the last 10 epochs. A seat named falcon with R = 20 carries 400 weight. If its operator splits that history into 10 clones, opal, cedar and eight more, each with R = 2, the ring holds 10 x 4 = 40, a 90% loss. Passes never transfer between keys, so every clone must earn each pass alone, and stacking a panel costs the attacker more real work than voting honestly as one seat.
